test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 7 July 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Which of the given statements is correct?

I. When Alivardi Khan died in 1756, Siraj-ud-daulah became the nawab of Bengal.

II. In 1757, Robert Clive led the company’s army against Siraj-ud-daulah at Plassey.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• At least **80 years old, Alivardi Khan **passed away from dropsy on **April 9, 1756, at 5 am.**
 
• **Siraj-ud-Daula**, his daughter's son, who was** 23** at the time, succeeded him.
 
• He was **Bengal's final Nawab** to rule on his own.
 
• The** East India Company **began to dominate over** Bengal **at the conclusion of his era.
 
• Siraj was enraged by the widespread abuse of** trade privileges by EIC authorities.**
 
• The** battle of Plassey in 1757 **was brought on by EIC's continued **wrongdoing **against Siraj-Ud-Daulah.
 
• On **June 23, 1757,** the Battle of Plassey took place in northeastern India.
 
• **Robert Clive's British East India Company **soldiers confronted Siraj-ud-Daulah, the last Nawab of Bengal, and his French allies.
 
• The head of Nawab's army,** Mir Jafar, **was bought off by Robert Clive with the promise of becoming the** Nawab of Bengal.**
 
• In **1757, Siraj-ud-Daulah **was beaten by **Clive at Plassey**, and **Calcutta **was taken.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Robert Clive:

 
 
• The** Bengal Presidency's first British governor** was Robert Clive.
 
• Clive is usually regarded as having laid the groundwork fo**r Bengali British East India Company** dominance.
 
• **Corruption** was rife during his** first term as governor of Bengal,** under Nawab Mir Jaffar.
 
• The business's only goal was to **maximize profits** at the expense of the** peasants.**
 
• In India, he accumulated a **sizable personal fortune** before departing for** London in 1760.**
 
• As **Bengal's Governor and Commander-in-Chie**f, he returned to India in 1765.
 
• In 1765, he founded a** "Society of Commerce**," but it was eventually disbanded.
 
• Bengal's king was now **Mir Qasim, the son-in-law **of Mir Jaffar.
